name: Brihadisvara Temple / தஞ்சைப் பெரிய கோவில்
info: Built by Raja Raja Chola I in 1010 CE, this architectural marvel is one of the largest South Indian temples and an outstanding example of fully realized Dravidian architecture. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site featuring a massive vimana and the largest monolithic Nandi.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple / மீனாட்சி அம்மன் கோவில்
info: A historic Hindu temple located on the southern bank of the Vaigai River. Dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi and Lord Sundareswarar. The temple complex is renowned for its 14 towering gopurams adorned with thousands of colorful mythological figures.

name: Shore Temple, Mamallapuram / மாமல்லபுரம்
info: A structural temple overlooking the Bay of Bengal, built during the reign of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II in the 8th century CE. It is part of the Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram (UNESCO World Heritage).

name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple / ஸ்ரீரங்கம்
info: The largest functioning Hindu temple complex in the world, dedicated to Lord Ranganatha. Spanning 156 acres with 21 majestic gopurams, it is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture located on an island enclosed by the Kaveri river.

name: Ramanathaswamy Temple / ராமேஸ்வரம்
info: Located on Pamban Island, this Jyotirlinga temple features the longest intricately carved sandstone corridor among all Hindu temples in India. Historically expanded by Pandya and Sethupathi kings.

name: Thillai Nataraja Temple / சிதம்பரம் நடராஜர் கோவில்
info: A cosmic temple dedicated to Lord Shiva as Nataraja, the Lord of Dance. It represents the space element (Akasha) of the Pancha Bhoota Sthalams, patronized heavily by the Cholas with golden roofs and bronze icons.

name: Airavatesvara Temple / ஐராவதேசுவரர் கோயில்
info: A 12th-century Chola temple at Darasuram built by Rajaraja Chola II. It is celebrated for its exquisite miniature stone sculptures and mandapams shaped like a chariot pulled by horses (UNESCO World Heritage).

name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram / கங்கைகொண்ட சோழபுரம்
info: Constructed by Emperor Rajendra Chola I as the capital of the Chola Empire in the 11th century. Features the magnificent Brihadisvara temple, similar to the one in Thanjavur but with a distinct feminine curve to its vimana.

name: Annamalaiyar Temple / அண்ணாமலையார் கோவில்
info: Nestled at the base of the Annamalai hills, this massive temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva representing the element of fire (Agni). Features immense gopurams constructed by Chola and Vijayanagara kings.

name: Ekambareswarar Temple / ஏகாம்பரநாதர் கோயில்
info: The largest temple in the city of Kanchipuram, representing the earth element (Prithvi). Notable for its lofty raja gopuram and the ancient mango tree under which Shiva and Parvati are believed to have married.

name: Nellaiappar Temple / நெல்லையப்பர் கோயில்
info: An expansive 7th-century CE temple complex built by the Pandyas. Known for its musical pillars that produce distinct musical notes when struck, and its beautifully carved stone structures.

name: Mangulam Inscriptions / மாங்குளம்
info: Home to the earliest dated Tamil-Brahmi rock-cut inscriptions (circa 3rd–2nd century BCE) recording rock beds gifted to Jain monks by the Pandya ruler Nedunchezhiyan.

name: Keezhadi / கீழடி
info: A major Sangam-era urban settlement excavated along the Vaigai river basin, dated scientifically to the 6th century BCE, revealing advanced brick structures, drainage systems, and Tamil-Brahmi potsherds.

name: Adichanallur / ஆதிச்சநல்லூர்
info: One of the most extensive ancient urn-burial sites in South India, dating back to 1000 BCE - 600 BCE. Excavations yielded iron implements, bronze artifacts, and gold diadems.
